# Japan by Station

> Carefully checked English guides to Japan travel, quick answer first: where to stay, what is within walking distance, local markets, nightlife, and how many minutes it takes to reach the airport, day trips and sights. Every time and price is checked against operators, airports and tourism bureaus, with the check date shown on each page.

## Station guides (start here)
- [Food Near Kyoto Station: Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner, Side by Side](https://japanbystation.com/food-near-kyoto-station): Hungry at Kyoto Station? Breakfast inside the gates from 6:30, ramen until 1:00 and a tofu dinner, by exit. Key facts (checked 2026-11-26): Breakfast: Shiokoji Cafe, inside the JR Central gate by Platform 0, opens 6:30 every day; Honke Daiichi Asahi ramen from 6:00 (closed Thursdays). Lunch: Shinpuku Saikan chuka soba ¥950 (9:00–20:00, cash only); Mimikou curry udon by the Karasuma East gate. Dinner: Kyo-tofu Fujino and Kyoto Obuya in Isetan 11F, 11:00–22:00. Facts checked 26 November 2026.
- [Food Near Osaka Station (Umeda): Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner and a Late Supermarket](https://japanbystation.com/food-near-osaka-umeda-station): Hungry at Osaka Station? Seven Umeda picks by meal, from 7:00 coffee to curry at 23:00, plus the supermarket by the gates. Key facts (checked 2026-11-26): Breakfast: Umeda Coffee-kan YC in Shin-Umeda Shokudogai, 2 min from JR Osaka, opens 07:00 every day (cash only). Lunch: Hanshin's ikayaki, B1 Snack Park, 10:00–22:00, under ¥200; Ekimae Building basements for udon and set lunches. Evening: Kyu Yamu Tetsudo spice curry in LUCUA B2 until 23:00; BIO-RAL supermarket by the Eki Marché gate 09:00–22:00. Facts checked 26 November 2026.
- [Food Near Shinjuku Station: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner and Late Night by Exit](https://japanbystation.com/food-near-shinjuku-station): Hungry at Shinjuku Station? Seven picks by exit and meal, from 6:20 soba to 24-hour ramen, with hours and prices. Key facts (checked 2026-11-26): Breakfast: Kameya soba, 2 min from the West Exit, opens 06:20 (Mon–Sat, cash only); Sawamura in NEWoMan serves breakfast 07:00–10:00. Lunch: Fuunji tsukemen ¥1,000 (11:00–15:00, 17:00–21:00, 6 min from the South Exit); Manna's Indian-style curry, served since 1927, ¥2,200. Late: Nagi in Golden Gai is open 24 hours; Keika ramen by the East Exit until 23:00. Facts checked 26 November 2026.
- [Hakata Station: Which Exit? Hakata vs Chikushi, Airport Subway, Ramen](https://japanbystation.com/hakata-station-which-exit): Hakata side or Chikushi side? Which exit for the bus terminal, Canal City and the airport subway, plus lockers, ramen and a saveable exit card. Key facts (checked 2026-11-25): Hakata exit (west): faces Tenjin; Hakata Bus Terminal about 1 min (city buses 1F, highway buses 3F), Canal City about 10 min on foot, KITTE and Hakata Hankyu. Chikushi exit (east): the airport-direction side; Yodobashi Hakata right outside, JR Kyushu Hotel Blossom Fukuoka about 2 min. Subway Airport Line: Hakata to Fukuoka Airport 2 stops, about 5 min, ¥260; to Tenjin about 5 min. Lockers: JR Kyushu lockers ¥400–1,200 by size; Multi E-Cube lockers with same-day hotel delivery. Checked 25 November 2026.
- [Kyoto Station Food Halls: The Classic Gift vs What Kyoto Buys](https://japanbystation.com/kyoto-station-depachika-gifts): Yatsuhashi or Saturday-only ohagi? Kyoto's three food halls, pair by pair, with the sweets that only arrive on set days. Key facts (checked 2026-11-25): JR Kyoto Isetan (inside Kyoto Station): 10:00–20:00; B1 sweets, sake and long-established shops, B2 fresh food, deli and bento; Eat Paradise 11F 11:00–22:00. Set-day sweets at Isetan B1 (Nov 2026): Imanishiken ohagi Saturdays from 11:00, 3 for ¥721; Nakamuraken mugite-mochi Thursdays and Sundays, 3 for ¥1,053. Takashimaya Kyoto 10:30–20:00, food on B1; Tsuruya Yoshinobu's Kyoto-only yokan 3 bars ¥1,274, keeps about a year.
- [Kyoto Station: Which Exit? Karasuma vs Hachijo, Buses, Lockers, Food](https://japanbystation.com/kyoto-station-which-exit): Karasuma side or Hachijo side? Which exit for buses, Kintetsu and the airport bus, plus lockers, ramen and a saveable exit card. Key facts (checked 2026-11-25): Karasuma (Central) exit, north: city bus terminal, Kyoto Tower, taxis, the Karasuma subway. Hachijo exit, south: Shinkansen side, Kintetsu to Nara, airport limousine buses (KIX ¥2,800, about 85–90 min). City bus: ¥230 flat fare; EX100/EX101 sightseeing express ¥500 from stop D1, weekends and holidays. Luggage: JR Central smart lockers on the Hachijo side from ¥400 a day; same-day hotel delivery if dropped by 11:00. Checked 25 November 2026.
- [Sapporo Station: Which Exit? South vs North, Chi-Ka-Ho to Odori, Airport Train](https://japanbystation.com/sapporo-station-which-exit): South or North exit? Which way for Odori, the airport train and the buses, plus lockers, food and a saveable exit card. Key facts (checked 2026-11-25): South exit: Daimaru, Stellar Place, the Chi-Ka-Ho underground walkway to Odori (about 520 m, about 10 min, open 5:45–24:30), the Clock Tower about 10 min on foot. North exit: Hokkaido University (West gates, about 7 min to the Main Gate) and the tour-bus stop. Rapid Airport to New Chitose: ¥1,230, fastest about 33–37 min; u-seat reserved car +¥1,000 (+¥800 ticketless). Buses: the station bus terminal closed on 30 Sep 2023; buses use temporary street stops around the South exit. Checked 25 November 2026.
- [Shin-Osaka vs Osaka Station: Which One, and Where to Stay](https://japanbystation.com/shin-osaka-vs-osaka-station): Bullet train or city base? Which station your train uses, the 11-minute transfer rule, and one hotel per traveller. Key facts (checked 2026-11-25): Two different stations: the Tokaido and Sanyo Shinkansen stop only at Shin-Osaka (platforms 20–27); Osaka Station (Umeda) has no Shinkansen platforms. They are one JR stop apart, about 4 minutes. Kyoto from either one: the JR Special Rapid starts at Osaka Station, calls at Shin-Osaka and reaches Kyoto in about 24 minutes from Shin-Osaka; the regular fare is ¥580 from both (JR West, checked 25 Nov 2026). Transfer time: JR West advises allowing 11 minutes to change from JR to the Osaka Metro Midosuji Line at Shin-Osaka (Umeda about 6 min, Namba about 16 min). Stay by traveller: early Shinkansen → remm Shin-Osaka (directly connected to the Shinkansen Central gate); families → Courtyard by Marriott Shin-Osaka Station (1 min, rooms from 30 m²); budget with a bath → Via Inn Shin-Osaka (3 min from the JR East Exit).
- [Namba Station: Which Namba, Which Exit for Your Hotel](https://japanbystation.com/namba-station-which-namba): Four stations called Namba: which one your train uses, which exit to take and where to sleep. Key facts (checked 2026-11-24): Four stations called Namba: Osaka Metro Namba (Midosuji M20, Yotsubashi Y15, Sennichimae S16), Nankai Namba (trains to Kansai Airport and Koyasan), Osaka-Namba (Kintetsu to Nara and Hanshin to Kobe, one shared station) and JR Namba (Yamatoji Line). All are linked on foot, mostly underground. To Kansai Airport: Nankai rapi:t from Nankai Namba, 34 min at the fastest; Airport Express about 45 min for the ¥970 base fare. Limousine bus from OCAT (JR Namba building) about 48 min to Terminal 1, ¥1,400 adult (checked 24 Nov 2026). Destination-first exits: Dotonbori → Osaka Metro Exit 14; Namba Parks and Nankai trains → Exit 4; Namba HIPS → Exit 15-B walkway; Kintetsu/Hanshin and Namba Walk → Exit 27 direction. Stay by traveller: airport by train → Swissotel Nankai Osaka (on top of Nankai Namba); airport bus, Nara or Kobe → Hotel Monterey Grasmere Osaka (1 min from JR Namba); nights out → Cross Hotel Osaka (3 min from Exit 14); rainy days and laundry → Namba Oriental Hotel (30 s from Namba Walk B21).
- [Osaka Station vs Umeda: Same Place? Which Side for Your Hotel](https://japanbystation.com/osaka-station-vs-umeda): Six stations, one hub: which one your train uses, where the airport bus stops, and the right side for your hotel. Key facts (checked 2026-11-24): Same hub, different stations: JR uses the name Osaka Station; Hankyu and Hanshin use Osaka-umeda (renamed from Umeda on 1 October 2019); Osaka Metro has Umeda, Higashi-Umeda and Nishi-Umeda. All are linked on foot. HARUKA to Kansai Airport: underground track 21 (track 24 towards Kyoto), nearest gate the West Gate. Airport bus to Kansai Airport: from Hankyu Sanbangai, about 60 min to Terminal 1, ¥1,800 adult one way, no reservation (Kansai Airport Transportation Enterprise, checked 24 Nov 2026). Stay by traveller: HARUKA arrivals → Osaka Station Hotel (West Gate); early trains → Hotel Granvia Osaka (Central Gate); families → Hotel Hankyu RESPIRE (3 min from the 3rd-floor bridge gate); budget → Nakazakicho, 800 m east.
- [Which "Asakusa Station" Will You Actually Use from Narita?](https://japanbystation.com/asakusa-which-station-from-narita): Asakusa's four stations, the direct Narita train, and the real walk to a 'near Asakusa Station' hotel. Key facts (checked 2026-11-25): Narita to Asakusa: Keisei's Access Express runs through onto the Toei Asakusa Line with no change: Narita Terminal 1 to Asakusa in about 70 minutes for ¥1,380 (Jorudan, checked 23 Nov 2026). Four stations, one name: Asakusa has Toei Asakusa Line, Ginza Line, Tobu and Tsukuba Express stations; no train from Narita reaches the Tsukuba Express station without changing (fastest: 72 minutes, ¥3,010, two changes). The luggage walk: from Toei exit A2b (step-free) to a hotel by the Tsukuba Express station is about 670 m, roughly 9 minutes, against about 240 m from TX exit A1. Tsukuba Express side: Akihabara in 5 minutes for ¥230; good for light packers heading to Akihabara, weak on arrival and departure days with big bags. Lift: the Ginza Line's Asakusa Exit 1 has a lift.

## Kyoto
- [Food Near Kyoto Station: Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner, Side by Side](https://japanbystation.com/food-near-kyoto-station): Hungry at Kyoto Station? Breakfast inside the gates from 6:30, ramen until 1:00 and a tofu dinner, by exit.
- [Kyoto in December 2026: Last Leaves, Temple Markets and the New Year Bells](https://japanbystation.com/kyoto-in-december-2026): No lantern path, but radish stew on 7–8 Dec, the year's last temple markets and bells you can ring on 31 Dec.
- [Kyoto Station Food Halls: The Classic Gift vs What Kyoto Buys](https://japanbystation.com/kyoto-station-depachika-gifts): Yatsuhashi or Saturday-only ohagi? Kyoto's three food halls, pair by pair, with the sweets that only arrive on set days.
- [Kyoto Station: Which Exit? Karasuma vs Hachijo, Buses, Lockers, Food](https://japanbystation.com/kyoto-station-which-exit): Karasuma side or Hachijo side? Which exit for buses, Kintetsu and the airport bus, plus lockers, ramen and a saveable exit card.
- [Fushimi Inari: Dawn, Afternoon or After Dark? How Far Up Is Worth It](https://japanbystation.com/fushimi-inari-dawn-day-or-after-dark): Dawn for empty torii, the afternoon only if you climb past Yotsutsuji, and after dark only on the lit lower paths.
- [Kansai Airport to Kyoto: Haruka, Limousine Bus or via Osaka?](https://japanbystation.com/kansai-airport-to-kyoto): Haruka for most arrivals, the bus when you land late or have big bags, Hankyu via Osaka when your hotel is on Shijo. Here's how to choose by where you sleep.
- [First Trip to Kyoto: Kyoto Station, Kawaramachi/Gion or Karasuma?](https://japanbystation.com/kyoto-where-to-stay-first-trip): Karasuma for most first trips: 3 minutes from Kyoto Station, one stop from Kawaramachi, Hankyu to Arashiyama. Kyoto Station for JR day trips; Gion for evenings.

## Osaka

- [Itami Sky Park: Can You Watch Planes Without a Car?](https://japanbystation.com/itami-sky-park-without-a-car): Hankyu to Itami + city bus 25 = ¥490 each way. Best day: go out via the airport deck, back via the bus.
- [Is NIFREL Worth a Two-Hour Trip?](https://japanbystation.com/nifrel-two-hours): Two hours inside: plenty. Two hours door to door: about 50 min inside from Umeda, under 30 from Namba.

- [Sakai: Can You Watch a Knife Being Made Without Booking?](https://japanbystation.com/sakai-watch-knife-making): Free sharpening demo every Friday 13:30–15:00, no booking. Forges want 10–15 days' notice.
- [Nakazakicho vs Umeda: Would You Walk for ¥3,000 Less a Night?](https://japanbystation.com/nakazakicho-vs-umeda-hotel): About ¥9,500 saved over three nights for a 12-minute walk. A taxi costs from ¥600.
- [Minoh Falls in Autumn: Leave Osaka at 1, Back Before Dark?](https://japanbystation.com/minoh-falls-autumn-afternoon): Umeda at 13:00 still works on a weekday: falls by 14:15, back before the 16:48 sunset. The shorter walk, and when to leave earlier.

- [Can ¥5,000 Buy a Private Room Near Namba?](https://japanbystation.com/namba-5000-yen-private-room): Wednesday: a private room from ¥2,998. Saturday: ¥5,000 buys a capsule. Real prices for two sampled nights.
- [Four Friends in Osaka: One Apartment or Two Hotel Rooms?](https://japanbystation.com/osaka-four-friends): Apartment, apartment hotel or two twins? What changes for four people, and how to check a rental is legal.
- [Where to Stay in Osaka If You're Out Late](https://japanbystation.com/osaka-night-owls): The subway stops around midnight. Stay where you can walk home: Namba, Ura-Namba or Tenma.
- [Where to Stay in Osaka to Live Like a Local](https://japanbystation.com/osaka-live-like-a-local): Tenma and Tsuruhashi: shopping streets, izakaya alleys and quiet mornings, still a few stops from Namba and Umeda.
- [Local Markets in Osaka Beyond Kuromon](https://japanbystation.com/osaka-local-markets): Kizu, Tsuruhashi and Japan's longest shopping street: where Osaka shops for dinner, with hours and closing days.
- [Tenma & Tenjinbashisuji: Where Osaka Locals Actually Eat](https://japanbystation.com/tenma-tenjinbashisuji-local-guide): Japan's longest shopping street, sushi at counter prices and standing bars after six: Osaka's local side, one stop from Osaka Station.
- [Where to stay in Osaka: Namba, Umeda or Tennoji?](https://japanbystation.com/osaka-where-to-stay): Three areas on one red subway line. What's outside each door, and who each one suits.

## Tokyo
- [Food Near Shinjuku Station: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner and Late Night by Exit](https://japanbystation.com/food-near-shinjuku-station): Hungry at Shinjuku Station? Seven picks by exit and meal, from 6:20 soba to 24-hour ramen, with hours and prices.
- [Depachika 101: How Japan's Department-Store Food Halls Work](https://japanbystation.com/depachika-japan-food-halls-how-they-work): What's on each counter, when the stickers go on, where you can eat it, and the tax rule that changed in November 2026.
- [Isetan Shinjuku Food Hall: Would You Try These?](https://japanbystation.com/isetan-shinjuku-food-hall-what-to-buy): Prawn heads fried to a crunch, crackers sold twice a month, an Isetan-only pudding: Tokyo's most famous food basement, oddest first.
- [Tokyo Christmas Markets 2026: Which One Is for You?](https://japanbystation.com/tokyo-christmas-markets-2026): Shin-Toyosu, Shiba Park, Roppongi Hills, Skytree or Yokohama: 2026 dates, hours, entry and which one to pick.
- [Hakone 'Private Onsen': Which Booking Actually Gets You One?](https://japanbystation.com/hakone-private-onsen-which-booking): An 'open-air bath' room isn't always hot-spring water. How to pick between an in-room bath, a reservable private bath and a two-hour private bath room in Yumoto.
- [Enoshima Without the Stairs: Escalator, Boat or Stay on the Shore?](https://japanbystation.com/enoshima-without-the-stairs): What the paid escalator really covers, the boat that saves the climb back, and a flat shore day with an island view.
- [Gora to Lake Ashi: Bus or Ropeway?](https://japanbystation.com/gora-to-lake-ashi-bus-or-ropeway): The ropeway is the view; the bus is the shortcut. From Gora, Lake Ashi and the shrine torii are only 20–30 minutes away by bus. Here's how to mix the two.
- [Kamakura From Noon: Temples, Sunset or Both?](https://japanbystation.com/kamakura-from-noon-temples-or-sunset): Hase's temples close around 16:30, the sun sets around then in winter and Hachimangu stays open to 20:00. Do them in that order.
- [Hakone Freepass for a Ryokan Night: Worth It or Not?](https://japanbystation.com/hakone-freepass-ryokan-one-night): Ryokan plus one short outing: skip the pass and save about ¥3,400. Ropeway and boat in the plan: the pass wins by about ¥1,200.
- [One Car-Free Night in Hakone: Yumoto, Gora or Lake Ashi?](https://japanbystation.com/hakone-base-yumoto-gora-lake-ashi): Yumoto for late arrivals and easy dinners, Gora for the museum and ropeway side, Lake Ashi for a quiet morning if you arrive by afternoon.
- [Hakone Ryokan With Dinner: What Time Should You Leave Tokyo?](https://japanbystation.com/hakone-ryokan-dinner-leave-tokyo): For an 18:00 ryokan check-in in Gora, take the 15:00 Romancecar; add the Open-Air Museum on the 10:00; or go room-only in Yumoto and eat out by 21:30.
- [Cloudy Fuji Forecast: Move the Kawaguchiko Trip, Go Anyway or Keep the Night?](https://japanbystation.com/kawaguchiko-cloudy-fuji-forecast): Move the date if your bookings allow it, keep the day with a museum-and-hoto plan, or keep the night for a second look next morning.
- [Lake Kawaguchi by Bike in Half a Day: How Far Can You Ride?](https://japanbystation.com/lake-kawaguchi-half-day-cycling): Catching the 14:58 train? Ride to the bridge and back. Got until 16:48? Take the north shore to Oishi Park. Windy? The Red Line bus does it in 27 minutes.
- [Tokyo to Kawaguchiko With a Big Suitcase: Bus or Train?](https://japanbystation.com/tokyo-to-kawaguchiko-big-suitcase-bus-or-train): Bus ¥2,000 with your case in the hold, the direct train ¥4,200 with only four or five morning runs, or the Kaiji via Otsuki when those are full.
- ['Mount Fuji View' Rooms at Lake Kawaguchi: What You Actually Buy](https://japanbystation.com/kawaguchiko-fuji-view-room-what-you-buy): Only a room type that says Mt. Fuji View is a promise. A Fuji name or a room picked at check-in is not. The free option: a ¥14,910 twin and the bridge at dawn.
- [Lake Kawaguchi Without a Car: Station Hotel, North Shore or Lakeside Ryokan?](https://japanbystation.com/lake-kawaguchi-station-or-lake-view): Station inn ¥13,200 and dinner by 19:00, north shore with a 17:45 last bus, or a lakeside ryokan where Fuji view and dinner cost extra.
- [Big Suitcase and One Night in Hakone: Forward It, Carry It or Store It?](https://japanbystation.com/hakone-big-suitcase-forward-carry-store): Send it straight to Kyoto for ¥3,160, hand it to Hakone's luggage desk at Yumoto, or lock it at Odawara for two days.
- [Tokyo Disney: Book the Hotel Night Before or After Your Park Day?](https://japanbystation.com/tokyo-disney-hotel-night-before-or-after): Disney hotel: the night before (Happy Entry). Official hotel: the night after. Same-date prices vs a Hatchobori base.
- [Kiyosumi-Shirakawa as a Tokyo Base: Quiet Mornings, but Breakfast at Seven?](https://japanbystation.com/kiyosumi-shirakawa-base-7am-start): Breakfast by 7:00, a slow 8:00 coffee, or a 6:30 buffet above the station: which morning fits a 7 a.m. start.

- [Shibuya Crossing: Is It Worth Paying to See It From Above?](https://japanbystation.com/shibuya-crossing-view): Free from Hachiko Square, a drink for the Starbucks window, ¥1,800 for the MAG8 rooftop or ¥2,700+ for Shibuya Sky. Which view fits you.
- ["Shinjuku" on the Booking: Which Station Will You Actually Use?](https://japanbystation.com/shinjuku-which-station): JR Shinjuku, Shinjuku-sanchome or Higashi-shinjuku? Same-night prices and the trips each one makes easy.
- [Narita or Haneda: Which Train Gets You to Your Tokyo Hotel Fastest?](https://japanbystation.com/tokyo-airport-which-train): Keikyu, Monorail, N'EX or Skyliner? Official times and fares, matched to where your hotel is.
- [Getting Around Tokyo: IC Card, JR or Metro, and Is the Subway Pass Worth It?](https://japanbystation.com/tokyo-ic-card-or-subway-pass): Suica, JR vs Metro, and the exact number of rides a day where the Tokyo Subway Ticket pays off.
- [First Trip to Tokyo: Which Area Should You Stay In?](https://japanbystation.com/tokyo-where-to-stay-first-trip): Shinjuku, Tokyo Station or Asakusa/Ueno? Same-night prices for two and the trips each base makes easy.

## Fukuoka
- [Fukuoka Food Beyond Tonkotsu Ramen: Eat It Like a Local](https://japanbystation.com/fukuoka-food-beyond-tonkotsu-ramen): Udon soft on purpose, mackerel raw, noodles in the hotpot at the end: Fukuoka eats differently.
- [Fukuoka Yatai: How They Work, and Nakasu, Tenjin or Nagahama?](https://japanbystation.com/fukuoka-yatai-how-they-work): About 100 stalls, ten seats each, mostly cash: how Fukuoka's yatai work, which area to pick and a three-stall evening.
- [Hakata Station: Which Exit? Hakata vs Chikushi, Airport Subway, Ramen](https://japanbystation.com/hakata-station-which-exit): Hakata side or Chikushi side? Which exit for the bus terminal, Canal City and the airport subway, plus lockers, ramen and a saveable exit card.
- [First Trip to Fukuoka: Hakata, Tenjin or Nakasu?](https://japanbystation.com/fukuoka-where-to-stay-first-trip): The airport is 5 minutes from Hakata by subway. Hakata for trains, Tenjin for shopping, Nakasu for yatai nights, and why all three work.

## Nagoya
- [Nabana no Sato Illumination 2026: Dates, Tickets and the Day Trip from Nagoya or Osaka](https://japanbystation.com/nabana-no-sato-illumination-2026): Japan's big light tunnel near Nagoya: 2026 dates, ticket prices with the ¥1,000 voucher, and the bus or Kintetsu set ticket to get there.

## Hokkaido
- [Otaru from Sapporo: Half Day or Overnight?](https://japanbystation.com/otaru-from-sapporo-half-day-or-overnight): 41 minutes from Sapporo: in winter a half day catches the lamps at four; in summer, stay the night.
- [Sapporo in December 2026: White Illumination and the Christmas Market](https://japanbystation.com/sapporo-in-december-2026): Odori's lights and the Munich Christmas Market until 25 December, plus the new Red Brick and Nakajima Park venues.
- [Sapporo Station: Which Exit? South vs North, Chi-Ka-Ho to Odori, Airport Train](https://japanbystation.com/sapporo-station-which-exit): South or North exit? Which way for Odori, the airport train and the buses, plus lockers, food and a saveable exit card.
- [New Chitose Airport to Sapporo: Train, Bus or Car?](https://japanbystation.com/new-chitose-airport-to-sapporo): The train is fastest and Suica works. The bus wins when it stops at your hotel door. A car only makes sense if Sapporo isn't your last stop.
- [Where Sapporo Locals Eat: Markets, Soup Curry and Ramen](https://japanbystation.com/sapporo-where-locals-eat): Curb Market for breakfast if you can get there early, soup curry in a basement off Odori, and ramen at 1 a.m. like Susukino does.
- [First Trip to Sapporo: Sapporo Station, Odori or Susukino?](https://japanbystation.com/sapporo-where-to-stay-first-trip): Odori for most first trips, Sapporo Station for early trains and big bags, Susukino if dinner runs late. All three are joined underground.

## Hiroshima
- [Hiroshima and Miyajima in One Day: Where to Base, Tram or Train, and the Tides](https://japanbystation.com/hiroshima-miyajima-one-day): Museum at 7:30, JR and ferry to the island by late morning, and one tide-table check that decides whether the torii floats or you can walk to it.

## Okinawa
- [Naha First Trip: Where to Stay and Do You Need a Car?](https://japanbystation.com/naha-where-to-stay-do-you-need-a-car): Stay near Kokusai-dori and ride the monorail in Naha. Rent a car only for the days you head north.

## Nara
- [Nara: Day Trip or One Night? Deer, Trains and a Quiet Evening](https://japanbystation.com/nara-day-trip-or-one-night): A day trip covers the big three before they close at five. One night buys Nigatsudo at sunset, quiet Naramachi and the deer before the crowds.
